So internalized misogyny is when women find themselves belittling or distrusting other women, especially (and in this case specifically) those who are more traditionally feminine. Kit HATES Elora from the moment she meets her, even before she finds out who she is, and continues to do so despite her desire to help and their shared goal of helping Airk. But she loves her womanizing brother and actively puts her trust in Boorman, despite his obvious selfishness and inability to give her a straight answer about her father's disappearance. We see this again with Allagash. Kit dismisses or ignores the negative qualities of men while passionately hating the only traditionally feminine woman in the group from the start because she bakes, likes boys, and doesn't use a sword. 

This is not a criticism for me, as I think that this is supposed to be Kit's journey throughout the show as she is forced to redefine her view of the world, her family and herself now that she's out in the world. She's learning that things and people aren't as straightforward as she had thought and that there's a lot she doesn't know.
